planting.note: Start seed indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost, soaking overnight to speed germination, then transplant onto a trellis, obelisk, or hanging basket after danger of frost has passed; in zones 9-11 it persists as a woody perennial.

directions: Alba is an old heirloom selection of black-eyed Susan vine, noted in Curtis's Botanical Magazine as far back as the 1830s, that is grown for pure creamy-white flowers lacking the dark central eye spot typical of the species. The clean white blooms stand out against the twining vine's heart-shaped foliage and make an effective pairing with the darker-centered orange and yellow forms on a shared trellis or mixed hanging basket. It shares the species' fast, twining growth and heat tolerance, flowering continuously from early summer through frost in a sunny spot with evenly moist, well-drained soil. Pinch young plants to encourage branching and deadhead spent flowers lightly to keep the display tidy and maximize repeat bloom.

planting.note: Set out container-grown starts after danger of frost has passed onto a trellis, obelisk, or large hanging basket in rich, well-drained soil; this vigorous selection quickly covers more support than compact Susie-series plants, so give it ample room to climb.

directions: Orange A-Peel is a modern, larger-flowered black-eyed Susan vine selection bred for unmarked, solid orange blooms rather than the dark central eye that gives the species its common name, giving plantings a brighter, more uniform flower color from a distance. Growth is notably vigorous and continuous-blooming, covering a trellis, arch, or tall obelisk from planting through the first fall frost without deadheading. It tolerates heat and humidity as well as the species type and performs equally well trained upright or allowed to cascade from a tall container or hanging basket. Site it in full sun with consistent moisture and a light monthly feeding for the densest cover and heaviest bloom.

planting.note: Plant container-grown vines after last frost on a trellis, arbor, or sturdy fence in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; where winters bring hard freezes, grow in a large container that can be moved to shelter.

directions: Spanish jasmine is a larger-flowered, twining relative of common jasmine long cultivated in the south of France and North Africa for the perfume trade, where its intensely fragrant white blossoms, often tinged pink in bud, are prized above nearly every other jasmine for essential oil quality. In the landscape it climbs vigorously onto any sturdy support, producing loose clusters of bloom from summer into fall on a semi-evergreen to deciduous vine with glossy pinnate foliage. It wants full sun to light afternoon shade and fertile, well-drained soil with regular moisture through the growing season, plus a post-bloom pruning to control its size and keep flowering wood renewed. Established plants tolerate brief dips into the upper 20s°F but are killed back hard by a freeze, so Gulf Coast gardeners outside the mildest coastal pockets should treat it as a root-hardy perennial or grow it in a movable container.

planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens after last frost in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, either against a trellis or fence to climb or left unsupported as a dense mounding hedge or ground cover.

directions: Wax jasmine is an Australian species valued in warm-climate landscapes for its small, glossy, thick-textured leaves and pinwheel-shaped white flowers that open from spring into fall with a light, sweet fragrance. Unlike many twining jasmines it is just as happy sheared into a dense mounding shrub or informal hedge as it is trained up a trellis or fence, making it a flexible choice for foundation plantings, screens, or containers. It takes full Gulf Coast sun and heat in stride and establishes best in well-drained soil with regular watering during its first growing season, tapering off once roots are established. Mature plants tolerate brief exposure to the low 30s°F but benefit from a sheltered site or mulch protection in the coolest parts of its hardiness range.
